facts.fact: An oil filter housing (cartridge) cap exists on the N52 and is removed from above/engine bay to change the filter
facts.summary: Several independent guides/parts sellers describe a cartridge-style housing with a removable cap and a dedicated cap socket/wrench listed for N52. Exact position on the engine (side/front/rear) is NOT stated by any fetched source; see fact 8.

sources.establishes: Filter cap sits on the housing in the engine bay and comes off with an oil-filter cap socket (article does not name N52).
E90 N52 uses a cartridge-style filter housing removed with a 26mm hex cap socket.
N52 DIY: remove the oil filter housing cap with a cap wrench, drop in new cartridge with two O-rings, refit until marks align.
Cap tool listed as fitting N52 (among others), confirming a cap-type housing on N52.
Bentley page title/abstract confirms an oil filter housing on N52/N54/N55 3-Series; body procedure was paywalled, no location text retrieved.

facts.fact: Where the filter housing cap is on the engine (side/front/rear; reachable from above)
facts.summary: No fetched source states which side/end of the N52 the cap is on. FCP says only 'engine bay'. No RealOEM/ETK exploded view was reachable via search results. Do not illustrate a specific side.

sources.establishes: Only that the cap is in the engine bay on the housing; no side given.

facts.fact: Oil filler cap location on N52
facts.summary: Cap is on the valve cover at the filler neck (top of engine). Which side/end of the valve cover is not stated by sources; do not draw a specific side.

sources.establishes: Filler cap sits on the valve cover at the filler neck; fitment lists E90 325i/330i and N52 cars.
N52 DIY: open the fill cap on the valve cover to help the oil drain.
General E90 DIY: with bonnet open remove filler cap before draining (engine type not named).

facts.fact: Oil drain plug location on pan and count
facts.summary: One drain plug on the underside of the pan, 17mm hex, reached through a small hatch/access panel near the front-center of the underside. Orientation/side conflicts: one source says slightly left of center on driver's side and faces right; another says it points straight down. Single plug is implied, never explicitly counted. Illustrate underside, near front-center, side unspecified.

sources.establishes: N52: drain plug is behind a small removable access panel on the underside; one poster says slightly left of center (driver side); orientation reports differ (down vs right); links a RealOEM diagram (not retrieved).
N52 plug is 17mm and sits vertically so oil drops straight down.
E90: small hatch behind front-centre jack point; plug is 17mm socket.
17mm plug with copper crush washer; oil exits sideways.

facts.fact: Whether undertray must come off for drain plug and its fasteners
facts.summary: Full tray removal is NOT required: E90 has a small access hatch/flap in the undertray (bimmerpost: removing the tray is cleaner but the flap works). Fastener type CONFLICTS: one source says hatch held by three screws; another says coin-operated hatch. No source gives counts/types for the full undertray. Illustrate only a small access hatch, no fastener count.

sources.establishes: Access panel held by three screws.
Small hatch opened with a coin.
Service flap works but removing undertray gives cleaner access; fasteners not listed.
OE belly pan exists (51757129341) and aftermarket replacement has an integrated access door to the drain plug.

facts.fact: Decorative plastic engine cover over N52 must come off to reach filter cap
facts.summary: No fetched source says whether an engine cover exists on the N52 or must be removed. Do not illustrate a cover.

facts.fact: Dash-based electronic oil level check menu path on E90
facts.summary: Instrument cluster via turn-signal stalk button: ignition on, press stalk button until OIL shows, then press end button to read level (OK / +1 qt). Sources are low-authority third-party. iDrive path NOT established (one bimmerpost poster says the oil level entry was absent from iDrive and had to be coded; another thread says iDrive or stalk computer after run). Illustrate cluster/stalk only.

sources.establishes: Press stalk button until cluster shows OIL, press end button, read OK or +1 qts (ignition on).
Check via trip computer/BC button and stalk (engine oil menu); sources disagree whether engine should be warm/running.
iDrive oil-level entry may be missing unless coded; reading unreliable; iDrive only shows low-oil warnings.
No mechanical dipstick; check level with iDrive or stalk computer after run.

facts.fact: Oil service (CBS) reset steps on E90
facts.summary: Ignition on (engine off); hold the trip/odometer reset button on the cluster ~5 s until service display appears; cycle to oil; hold until RESET appears and confirms. FCP uses stalk BC button to scroll/hold; USRO says press/hold the same cluster button (~3 s) at RESET?. USRO also lists an iDrive path (Vehicle Info > Service Info > Engine Oil > Reset) as a single-source item.

sources.establishes: Doors closed, ignition on no start, hold cluster reset button ~5 s, scroll to oil with stalk, hold BC button until RESET and confirmation.
Hold trip-reset button ~5 s to service icon, cycle to oil icon, hold ~3 s at RESET?; alt iDrive Vehicle Info > Service Info > Engine Oil > Reset.
